name: Arepa Döner Sliders
style: Colombian arepa × Turkish döner street snack
description: Mini Colombian arepas stuffed with sliced Turkish döner, topped with aji criollo and garlic yogurt sauce, served as bite-size sliders.
ingredients: Aji criollo sauce (onion, cilantro, chili, lime)
preparation: Lightly toast or grill the mini arepas until the outside is slightly crisp.
Reheat the döner in a pan briefly so it becomes hot and slightly caramelized.
Slice each arepa horizontally like a slider bun.
Fill with hot döner slices, then spoon aji criollo and garlic yogurt sauce on top.
Finish with fresh cilantro or parsley and serve as bite-size sliders with lime wedges.
taste_profile: Rich, fatty umami from the döner
Fresh, tangy and slightly spicy notes from aji criollo
Comforting, familiar bar flavor from the garlic yogurt sauce
Warm corn arepa texture as a soft, slightly sweet base
menu_blurb: Mini Colombian arepas stuffed with Turkish döner, topped with aji criollo and garlic yogurt – perfect bite-size sliders for the bar.

name: Bandeja Antioquia Burger
style: Burger inspired by Colombian bandeja with Turkish twists
description: A juicy burger patty layered with red bean mash, roasted eggplant–tomato relish and Turkish white cheese, bringing the spirit of Bandeja Paisa into a burger.
ingredients: Turkish white cheese (as queso costeño substitute)
Optional: jalapeño or hot chili slices
preparation: Season the burger patty with salt, pepper and a little cumin, then grill or pan-sear until cooked to your preferred doneness.
Prepare a spiced red bean mash by cooking red beans with garlic, cumin and a touch of chili, then mashing to a spreadable texture.
Dice roasted eggplant and cook briefly with tomato sauce to make a rustic relish.
Lightly toast the burger bun.
Spread bean mash on the bottom bun, place the patty on top, then add slices of white cheese and the eggplant–tomato relish.
Finish with lettuce and onion rings, close the bun and serve with fries.
taste_profile: Deep, hearty flavors inspired by Bandeja Paisa (beans + grilled meat)
Smoky sweetness from roasted eggplant and tomato
Salty creaminess from Turkish white cheese
A rich, comforting burger that feels both Colombian and Turkish
menu_blurb: Beef burger with spiced red bean mash, roasted eggplant–tomato relish and Turkish white cheese – a Bandeja Paisa inspired burger.

name: Aegean–Colombian Cheese Paçanga
style: Aegean herb & cheese börek with tropical guava
description: Crispy paçanga börek stuffed with Aegean herbs and a mix of Turkish white cheese and queso costeño/cheddar, finished with a light guava drizzle for a sweet–savory signature contrast.
ingredients: Yufka or pastry sheets for paçanga
Queso costeño or salty Turkish white cheese, crumbled
Fresh Aegean herbs (mixed – e.g. wild greens, rocket etc.)
A small pinch of finely chopped sage
Finely chopped jalapeño or green chili
Guava purée or guava sauce for topping
preparation: Crumble the white cheese and mix with grated kashar in a bowl.
Finely chop the Aegean herbs, thyme, sage and dill; fold into the cheese mixture.
Add a little finely chopped jalapeño for a Colombian heat note.
Cut the pastry into rectangles, place the filling and roll tightly into paçanga logs.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Plate the böreks and drizzle a thin line of guava sauce over the top. Sprinkle with sesame or nigella seeds if desired.
taste_profile: Salty, aromatic cheese-and-herb filling reminiscent of the Aegean coast
Tropical, lightly sweet contrast from the guava drizzle
Gentle heat from jalapeño
Very crispy outside, soft cheesy interior
menu_blurb: Crispy Aegean börek stuffed with mixed cheeses and herbs, finished with a tropical guava drizzle – our signature fusion snack.

name: Patacón Kokoreç Taco
style: Fried green plantain base topped with Turkish kokoreç
description: Crispy fried green plantain slices (patacón) used as a base for finely chopped kokoreç and spicy Colombian hogao sauce – a bold bar plate.
ingredients: Ground cumin, dried thyme and chili flakes
Fresh cilantro or parsley, lime wedges
preparation: Deep-fry the plantain slices until lightly golden, then flatten them gently and fry again until very crisp to make patacón.
Sauté the chopped kokoreç in a pan with cumin, thyme and chili flakes.
Prepare hogao sauce separately by cooking tomato, onion and cilantro until slightly thickened.
Top each patacón with the hot kokoreç and a spoonful of hogao.
Garnish with fresh herbs and serve immediately with lime wedges.
taste_profile: Crispy, slightly sweet-starchy base from fried plantain
Intense, spicy offal flavor from kokoreç
Fresh, tangy and lightly hot notes from hogao
High-impact, very bar-friendly snack
menu_blurb: Crispy green plantain “tacos” topped with Turkish kokoreç and hogao – crunchy, spicy and addictive.

name: Empanada Sigara Roll
style: Colombian empanada filling inside Turkish sigara börek
description: Thin sigara börek pastry filled with Colombian-style minced beef empanada mix and melted kashar cheese, served with salsa rosada and spicy Turkish pepper sauce.
ingredients: Yufka cut into triangles for sigara böreği
Empanada mince filling (ground beef, onion, garlic, cumin, pepper, tomato)
preparation: Prepare a classic empanada filling by cooking minced beef with onion, garlic, tomato and spices; let it cool slightly.
Place some filling and grated kashar at the wide edge of each pastry triangle.
Roll tightly into a thin cylinder and seal the tip with a little water.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden and crisp, then drain well.
Serve hot with salsa rosada and spicy pepper sauce on the side.
taste_profile: Savory, gently spiced empanada mince
Melty, stretchy cheese in the center
Very crisp, thin pastry shell
Creamy and spicy contrast from the two sauces
menu_blurb: Crispy Turkish sigara böreği filled with Colombian empanada mince and cheese, served with salsa rosada and spicy pepper sauce.

name: Crispy Falafel – Aji Criollo Dip
style: Turkish-style falafel with Colombian aji–tahini dip
description: Chickpea falafel balls served with a creamy dip made from aji criollo, tahini and lime. A fully vegan bar plate.
ingredients: Ground cumin, coriander seeds, salt and black pepper
preparation: Blend chickpeas, onion, garlic, herbs and spices in a food processor; add flour if needed until the mixture holds its shape.
Form small falafel balls and chill briefly.
Deep-fry in hot oil until dark golden and very crisp.
For the dip, whisk together aji criollo, tahini, lime juice and a little olive oil until smooth.
Serve the hot falafel with plenty of aji-tahini-lime dip.
taste_profile: Warm, earthy flavor from chickpeas and spices
Creamy, rich body from the tahini-based dip
Fresh, tangy and slightly spicy notes from aji and lime
Vegan but very filling and bar-friendly
menu_blurb: Crispy chickpea falafel served with a creamy aji criollo–tahini–lime dip – 100% vegan, 200% flavor.

name: Bandeja Anatolia Nachos
style: Lavash chips loaded with Turkish & Colombian toppings
description: Crispy lavash chips topped with bean mash, spiced minced beef, melted cheese, yogurt chili sauce, hogao and roasted eggplant – a sharing nachos platter.
ingredients: Oil for frying or olive oil for baking
preparation: Fry or bake lavash triangles until crunchy to make chips.
Spread chips in a baking dish, then spoon bean mash and hot minced beef over them.
Top with grated cheese and bake briefly until melted.
Remove from the oven and drizzle hogao, roasted eggplant and yogurt chili sauce over the top.
Garnish with fresh herbs and serve with lime wedges.
taste_profile: Light Turkish character from lavash chips
Bandeja-style richness from beans and mince
Tangy, spicy and creamy combination of hogao and yogurt chili sauce
Perfect for large sharing platters
menu_blurb: Lavash nachos loaded with bean mash, spiced mince, melted cheese, hogao, roasted eggplant and spicy yogurt sauce.

name: Çöp Şiş Anticucho
style: Turkish çöp şiş with Colombian anticucho glaze
description: Grilled Turkish çöp şiş marinated in anticucho-style spicy sauce, served with fries and garlic–thyme yogurt dip.
ingredients: Anticucho-style sauce (chili, garlic, vinegar, cumin, paprika)
preparation: Marinate the meat pieces in anticucho sauce for at least 1–2 hours.
Thread onto skewers and grill on high heat until nicely charred on the outside.
Prepare fries as a side.
For the dip, mix yogurt with grated garlic, chopped thyme and a little lemon juice.
Serve the skewers with fries and the yogurt dip on the side.
taste_profile: Vinegary, chili-forward and smoky notes from anticucho marinade
Familiar Turkish grilled meat texture and flavor
Cooling, creamy balance from the herb yogurt dip
Very satisfying bar plate with fries
menu_blurb: Grilled çöp şiş skewers in a spicy anticucho marinade, served with fries and garlic–thyme yogurt dip.

name: Arepa Lahmacun
style: Thin arepa wraps with lahmacun filling
description: Thin arepa bases spread with lahmacun mince, rolled into mini pinwheels and served with nar ekşisi–lime glaze and fresh cilantro.
ingredients: Thin arepa bases or corn tortillas
Lahmacun mince (ground beef, tomato, onion, pepper, parsley, spices)
preparation: Heat the arepa bases lightly so they become flexible.
Spread a thin layer of lahmacun mince over each base.
Roll tightly and slice into bite-size pinwheels.
Bake briefly until the mince is cooked and the outside takes a little color.
Before serving, drizzle with a mix of nar ekşisi and lime juice, and garnish with fresh cilantro.
taste_profile: Classic Turkish lahmacun spice profile
Corn-based, slightly sweet arepa base
Sweet–sour notes from pomegranate molasses and lime
Easy-to-share finger food
menu_blurb: Thin arepa rolls filled with lahmacun mince, finished with nar ekşisi–lime glaze and fresh cilantro.

name: Empanada Mantı Bites
style: Mini empanadas with Turkish mantı filling
description: Mini empanada shells filled with classic Turkish mantı mince, fried until crisp and served with garlic yogurt and a spicy ají drizzle.
ingredients: Mantı mince (beef, onion, black pepper, salt)
Butter or oil with chili flakes
preparation: Place a small spoonful of mantı mince in the center of each empanada disc.
Fold over and seal the edges tightly to form mini empanadas.
Fry in hot oil or bake until golden and crisp.
Prepare garlic yogurt and a warm chili butter or ají drizzle.
Plate the bites, spoon yogurt on top and finish with the chili drizzle and parsley.
taste_profile: All the flavor of classic mantı but in finger-food form
Crispy outside, juicy mince inside
Garlic yogurt and chili drizzle for creamy–spicy contrast
Familiar for Turkish guests, surprising for international visitors
menu_blurb: Mini empanadas stuffed with Turkish mantı mince, topped with garlic yogurt and a spicy ají drizzle.

name: Mondongo Kokoreç Fries
style: Loaded fries with kokoreç & mondongo spices
description: Crispy fries topped with kokoreç seasoned with mondongo-style spices and finished with smoky chipotle yogurt.
ingredients: Mondongo-style spice mix (cumin, garlic, cilantro, chili, etc.)
preparation: Fry the potatoes until very crispy.
Sauté the kokoreç with the mondongo spice mix until fragrant.
Mix yogurt with chipotle sauce to make a smoky, spicy yogurt.
Pile fries on a plate, top with hot kokoreç.
Drizzle with chipotle yogurt and garnish with chopped spring onion or cilantro.
taste_profile: Intense offal flavor from kokoreç
Smoky, spicy depth from mondongo spices and chipotle
Comforting base of crispy loaded fries
Creamy, tangy finish from the yogurt sauce
menu_blurb: Crispy fries loaded with kokoreç, mondongo spices and smoky chipotle yogurt drizzle.

name: Yuca Fries with Turkish Sucuk
style: Cassava fries with Turkish sucuk
description: Fried yuca sticks topped with sautéed Turkish sucuk pieces and a yogurt–lime–cilantro–ají sauce.
ingredients: Turkish sucuk, small cubes or slices
preparation: Parboil the yuca sticks in salted water, then drain and fry until crisp on the outside.
Sauté sucuk pieces in a pan until browned and slightly crispy.
Prepare a sauce by mixing yogurt with lemon/lime juice, chopped cilantro and a little ají.
Pile yuca fries on a plate, top with sucuk.
Drizzle with the yogurt–lime–cilantro sauce and serve immediately.
taste_profile: Crispy outside, soft inside texture of yuca fries
Smoky, spicy character of Turkish sucuk
Refreshing sauce with yogurt, citrus and cilantro plus gentle heat from ají
Very filling sharing plate
menu_blurb: Crispy cassava fries topped with Turkish sucuk and a cilantro–yogurt–lime–ají sauce.

name: Arequipe Lokma Bombs
style: Turkish lokma filled with Colombian arequipe
description: Turkish lokma doughnuts filled with Colombian arequipe (milk caramel) and rolled in coconut or crushed nuts – a snack-style dessert for the bar.
ingredients: Colombian arequipe (dulce de leche style caramel cream)
preparation: Prepare lokma dough and fry in hot oil into small round doughnuts.
While still warm, inject arequipe into the center using a piping bag with a narrow tip.
Roll the lokma in coconut or crushed nuts to coat the outside.
Dust lightly with icing sugar if desired and serve warm.
taste_profile: Crispy outside, soft and airy inside classic lokma texture
Rich, milky caramel flavor from the arequipe filling
Extra aroma and crunch from coconut or nuts
Perfect small dessert bite to pair with cocktails
menu_blurb: Warm Turkish lokma filled with Colombian arequipe and rolled in coconut or crushed nuts – the ideal snack dessert for the cocktail bar.

name: Aguardiente–Rakı Citrus Sour
style: Andean–Anatolian Citrus Sour
description: Colombian aguardiente and Turkish rakı meet in a bright, foamy citrus sour with orange bitters.
ingredients: Egg white or aquafaba (optional, for foam)
preparation: Add aguardiente, rakı, lemon juice, orange juice, simple syrup and egg white/aquafaba to a shaker.
Dry shake (without ice) for 8–10 seconds to create foam.
Add ice and shake again until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass.
Finish with a few drops of orange bitters on top of the foam.
taste_profile: Bright lemon–orange acidity with a soft sweetness.
Anise notes from aguardiente and rakı that appear in the finish.
Silky, foamy texture if egg white or aquafaba is used.

name: Turkish Bogotá Mojito
style: Bogotá–Istanbul Mojito Twist
description: A mojito where nar ekşisi replaces sugar and aguardiente brings a Colombian kick to classic mint and lime.
preparation: In a highball glass, gently muddle mint leaves with lime wedges and nar ekşisi.
Fill the glass with ice.
Add aguardiente and lime juice, then stir to combine.
Top with soda water and give a final gentle stir.
Garnish with fresh mint and a lime wheel.
taste_profile: Herbal mint and bright lime like a classic mojito.
Nar ekşisi adds deep, tangy pomegranate richness instead of simple sugar.
Light anise and spice from aguardiente in the aftertaste.

name: Saffron Margarita Colombiana
style: Saffron & Passion Fruit Margarita
description: Tequila, Colombian passion fruit and Turkish saffron infusion create a golden, aromatic margarita.
ingredients: 20 ml saffron-infused triple sec or Cointreau
10 ml agave syrup (optional, to balance acidity)
preparation: Rim a coupe or rocks glass with salt or chili-salt and fill with ice.
Add tequila, saffron-infused triple sec, passion fruit, lime juice and agave syrup into a shaker with ice.
Shake vigorously for 10 seconds.
Strain into the prepared glass.
Garnish with a lime wheel or a small pinch of saffron threads.
taste_profile: Intense tropical passion fruit acidity balanced by lime.
Warm, floral saffron aroma carried by the orange liqueur.
Classic margarita structure with an exotic, golden twist.

name: Granizado Ayran Vodka
style: Salty Ayran Vodka Slush
description: A salty ayran–based vodka slush with lime and mint, inspired by Turkish yogurt drinks and Latin granizados.
ingredients: 60 ml lightly salted ayran (Turkish yogurt drink)
preparation: In a blender, add ayran, vodka, lime juice, simple syrup and mint leaves.
Add plenty of crushed ice and blend until slushy.
Pour into a chilled highball or goblet glass.
Garnish with a mint sprig and a thin lime wheel.
taste_profile: Refreshing salty–sour yogurt base with lime brightness.
Herbal mint aroma, very drinkable despite the vodka.
Texture similar to a granizado or frozen margarita.

name: Arequipe Espresso Martini
style: Colombian–Turkish Coffee Martini
description: An espresso martini enriched with Turkish coffee aroma and Colombian arequipe caramel.
ingredients: 25 ml fresh espresso (or strong Turkish coffee)
15 ml arequipe (Colombian caramel) or dulce de leche
A pinch of very finely ground Turkish coffee (optional)
preparation: Add vodka, espresso, coffee liqueur and arequipe into a shaker.
Add plenty of ice and shake hard until the shaker is very cold and foamy.
Fine strain into a chilled martini glass.
Sprinkle a very small pinch of ground Turkish coffee or cocoa on top.
taste_profile: Intense coffee aroma with a caramelized sweetness from arequipe.
Silky, slightly creamy texture with a thick foam on top.
Subtle Turkish coffee bitterness balancing the sweetness.

name: Reggaeton Raki Highball
style: Rakı & Passion Highball
description: A long, bubbly highball where Turkish rakı meets soda, lime and a touch of maracuyá syrup.
preparation: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add rakı, passion fruit syrup and lime juice.
Top with cold soda water and give a gentle stir.
Garnish with a lime wheel; serve with a straw if desired.
taste_profile: Light anise character from rakı, lifted by lime and soda.
Gentle tropical sweetness from maracuyá syrup.
Very refreshing, easy-drinking highball for hot nights.

name: Tropical Şalgam Vodka
style: Spicy Şalgam Highball
description: Vodka and Turkish red şalgam juice with lime and chili salt for a spicy, savory highball.
ingredients: Pinch of chili salt or smoked chili powder for the rim
preparation: Rim a highball glass with lime and dip into chili salt.
Fill the glass with ice.
Add vodka, şalgam juice and lime juice.
Stir gently to combine.
Garnish with a lime wedge and, optionally, a chili slice.
taste_profile: Savory, slightly fermented character from şalgam.
Citrusy freshness from lime balancing the salt and spice.
Chili salt rim adds smoky heat on every sip.

name: Patacón Old Fashioned
style: Rum & Fried Plantain Old Fashioned
description: A smoky rum old fashioned infused with the aroma of crispy patacón (fried plantain skin).
ingredients: 1 bar spoon demerara sugar or simple syrup
Plantain peel or dried plantain chip for aroma
preparation: In a mixing glass, combine rum, sugar and bitters.
Add ice and stir until well chilled.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Express an orange peel over the drink and garnish.
Briefly flame or smoke a piece of plantain peel and present the drink with the aroma, or clip a dried plantain chip to the rim.
taste_profile: Deep molasses and oak notes from aged rum.
Bitters and demerara sugar create a classic old fashioned backbone.
Light fried-plantain aroma for a unique Colombian street-food reference; optionally smoky on the nose.

name: Tropical Ottoman Sherbet Cocktail
style: Ottoman Sherbet x Colombian Tropics
description: Traditional Turkish pomegranate/cherry sherbet fused with Colombian maracuyá and aguardiente or rum – a red–orange, tropical sherbet cocktail.
ingredients: 80 ml Turkish pomegranate or cherry sherbet
Lime slice, pomegranate seeds and fresh mint for garnish
preparation: Fill a shaker with ice.
Add sherbet, maracuyá, lemon juice and aguardiente/rum.
Shake vigorously for 8–10 seconds.
Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass or over fresh ice in a tumbler.
Finish with a few drops of orange bitters.
Garnish with a lime wheel, pomegranate seeds and a mint sprig.
taste_profile: Front: sweet–tart pomegranate or cherry sherbet.
Middle: tropical, fragrant maracuyá acidity.
Finish: gentle anise note from aguardiente and citrus bitterness from orange bitters – very drinkable but complex fusion.

name: Aegean Coastal Fire
style: Aegean Tropical Sherbet Cooler
description: Aegean-style lemon mint sherbet, Colombian passion fruit and a touch of aguardiente over rum – like an Aegean sea breeze meeting tropical fire.
ingredients: 70 ml Aegean-style lemon sherbet (lemon, fresh mint, light sugar)
Pomegranate seeds, lemon peel spiral and mint sprig for garnish
preparation: Add rum, aguardiente, lemon sherbet, maracuyá, honey and a few mint leaves into a shaker with ice.
Shake strongly for about 10 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice into a large goblet or highball glass.
Add 2–3 drops of rose water on top.
Garnish with a mint sprig, lemon peel spiral and a few pomegranate seeds.
taste_profile: First sip: cooling lemon sherbet and fresh mint – pure Aegean breeze.
Middle: passion fruit acidity bringing tropical energy.
Finish: gentle sweetness from honey and light anise notes from aguardiente, with a floral hint of rose water.

name: Sage & Lulo Breeze
style: Herbal Gin & Lulo Highball
description: A gin highball built on aromatic sage syrup and tangy Colombian lulo, topped with soda.
ingredients: 40 ml lulo juice (or lulo pulp diluted)
Mandarin or orange peel for garnish
preparation: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add gin, lulo juice and sage syrup.
Top with soda water and stir gently.
Garnish with a strip of mandarin or orange peel and a small sage leaf if available.
taste_profile: Aromatic herbal top notes from sage.
Refreshing, slightly sour lulo fruit body.
Dry, crisp finish supported by the botanicals of the gin.
